Remember Monkey Island? On Monkey Island, we discussed this previously. 100 people are transported onto an island randomly and they have to survive millions of flesh-eating monkeys. This experience makes them strong, wise, and united. They're transported back to the real world, and together they conquer the world.

The challenge now is how to ensure that my children and my grandchildren inherit my legacy. The answer is through ritual. So what you do is take your children, put them on an island, tell them a story, and then give them psychedelics.

Psychedelics enhance your experience so you actually believe the story is happening to you. It's like being in a movie. These rituals make you believe that you've experienced this yourself. This is programming. Every human brain can be programmed in a certain way.

Let's go back to the story. Rah represents the virtuous hero, Osiris the passive victim, and Horus the vengeanceful child. By doing these different rituals, I can get the pharaoh to believe he’s a different person in different circumstances. While the pharaoh is drugged up, dressed as Ra, he will take an effigy or a real person and stab, lance, burn, or strangle that person to feel like a virtuous hero. The pharaoh will also be asked to be Osiris, put in a tomb, cut up, and have sex with a prostitute.

This creates trauma which leads to disassociation, allowing the priest to program the pharaoh. Isis supports the pharaoh, calming him even having sex with him to make him dependent on her. Now Isis becomes the controller, the one the pharaoh will always trust.

If the priest wants to tell the pharaoh something, he can do it late at night while the pharaoh is sleeping or drugged up. The priest wearing the Isis mask can whisper instructions to the pharaoh. Different scents activate different identities. For example, incense for Ra and roses for Osiris. When the pharaoh is in the throne room and needs to make a decision, the priest releases scents that trigger emotions, determining how the pharaoh will decide.

We're all programmable. At school we're students; at home, children; outside, friends; at work, employees. Different circumstances activate different identities and behaviors. The pharaoh must be programmed to some degree.

To better understand this, imagine you are the best soccer player in the world but one day lose all your memory and forget who you are or what you do. The entire world forgets about you as well.
